I usually don’t write reviews, but I felt I should share my experience as a buyer in Avanya (Dynamix Avanya), Tower C.

When I initially booked, I was verbally told possession would be around December 2024. Over time, this kept getting pushed, and later I was told it would be delivered as per the RERA timeline of March 2026.

It’s now April 2026, and there is still no possession, no OC, and no clear written communication on the delay or revised timeline.

What’s more frustrating is the lack of transparency. I’ve been following up regularly on calls and emails, but most responses are vague or verbal, with no proper clarity in writing.

Meanwhile, I’m managing both EMI and rent, which is financially stressful. I understand delays can happen, but better communication and accountability would make a big difference.

If you’re considering this project Tower D, just make sure you track everything on RERA and get all commitments clearly in writing instead of relying only on verbal assurances.

🚨 A Builder’s Commitment Shouldn’t End at Sales 🚨

On 24th June 2025, a face-to-face meeting was held at Dynamix’s Head Office, Goregaon with 14–15 residents present. Embarrassing as it is, not a single commitment discussed has been acted upon till date.

Even worse, timelines mentioned in the meeting (6 weeks for society formation) were silently changed in emails to 3–4 months. If timelines can be altered so casually, what does that say about credibility?

Here’s what residents of Dynamix Avanya are still waiting on:
🔹 Society Formation & Final Handover
🔹 Transparency on Accounts – advance maintenance, infra costs collected but no amenities delivered
🔹 Conveyance Deeds & Title transfer to the society
🔹 Basic amenities & safety – lighting, cleanliness, solar heating, signage, water leakage in parking, stack parking pending
🔹 Security & staff management – fewer guards, mismanagement, and unacceptable resident experiences

Despite repeated follow-ups, fortnightly updates (promised in June) were never shared. The state of the project remains exactly the same as it was months ago.

And yet, Dynamix is gearing up to launch Tower D of Avanya.
👉 To new buyers: please ask yourself—if existing residents are struggling like this, what can you expect?

We, the current residents, invested our trust and life savings here. All we are asking for is delivery of what was promised—not delays, not shifting timelines, and not silence.

Accountability is not optional. It is the foundation of reputation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointed with false commitments – Avanya Tower C (Dynamix Group), Dahisar

I booked a flat in March 2023 at Avanya Tower C (Dynamix Group). At the time of booking, the sales team clearly committed possession by late 2024 or early 2025. Based on this assurance, I went ahead with the purchase.

However, once 2025 arrived, the commitments kept changing:

Initially, the CRM team informed me that possession would be given by Diwali 2025.

When I followed up again in July 2025, I was told possession would now be in March 2026, as per RERA timelines.

Recently, I was informed that they will apply for the Occupancy Certificate (OC) in March 2026 that is also not fixed, which realistically means another 3–4 months delay in possession after that.

This continuous change in timelines has been extremely frustrating. There is no transparency, and buyers are repeatedly given false or misleading commitments.

I have been staying on rent since 2025, hoping that I would finally get possession of my flat, but once again I am facing disappointment due to the builder’s delayed delivery and false assurances. This has caused significant financial and mental stress.

Overall, my experience with Dynamix Avanya has been very disappointing. I strongly advise prospective buyers to be very careful and not rely on verbal commitments made by the sales or CRM teams. Please ensure everything is clearly documented, as buyers are being misled with changing promises.

featured_reviews.name: SKR
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience with this project was disappointing and raised serious concerns regarding transparency, customer service, and sales practices.

During my interactions, I found that multiple representatives, including telecallers and CRMs, provided inconsistent information and commitments that were ultimately not fulfilled. I frequently received calls from different phone numbers, often with different names being used by the callers, despite having already visited the site and clearly communicated my requirements. The repeated follow-ups felt excessive and unprofessional.

One of my primary concerns was the inability to view a sample 3BHK apartment. Prospective buyers are shown a 2BHK model flat and expected to make a high-value purchase decision for a 3BHK unit without being able to inspect a representative layout. In my case, I was specifically assured that I would be shown a sample 3BHK unit in an under-construction building. However, after reaching the site, the CRM informed me that this would not be possible and cited various reasons, while attributing the misunderstanding to the telecaller. This created the impression that commitments were being made merely to secure site visits.
I also observed concerns raised by residents and reviewers regarding issues such as water supply, leakage, and stray animal management. While there are certainly some positive reviews and satisfied customers, prospective buyers should conduct thorough due diligence before making a decision.
Another concern was the noticeable change in customer engagement after the booking and registration stages, as several customers have reported a decline in responsiveness and support.

This is a large township project, and while it may suit some buyers, it is important to evaluate all aspects carefully. I would recommend comparing multiple projects and builders before making a significant investment, as there are other developments in the market known for greater transparency and customer-centric practices.
